To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PL intensity of ZnO:Ag films increases at aging, but PL intensities of other PL bands decrease.

the aging of ZnO:Ag films at 300 K leads to the formation of Ag–O bounds and oxygen interstitials, which are responsible for the increasing of PL intensity of the 2.10 eV PL band and the formation of the orange PL at aging.
the PL intensity of orange emission band increases at aging, while the PL intensity of UV emission band decreases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of Ag doping and the effect of aging on the PL spectra of ZnO NCs.
the formation and aging processes of Ag-doped ZnO NC films prepared by ultrasonically assisted spray pyrolytic deposition.
the nature of optical transitions in ZnO:Ag nanocrystals and the effect of Ag-doping and aging on the optical properties of these nanocrystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiative defect varying at aging is connected with the formation and variation of the oxygen interstitials and the substitutional AgZns defects.

the PL intensity of orange band in ZnO:Ag nanocrystals is connected with oxygen interstitials and Ag-O bounds formation at aging, but PL intensity of blue band is connected with substitutional AgZndoping.
the aging of ZnO:Ag nanocrystal films is accompanied by a decrease in the concentration of AgZn defects in ZnO:Ag, and an increase in the concentration of interstitial oxygen in ZnO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PL bands at 2.85 and 2.70 eV are connected with AgZn defects, the PL band at 3.18 eV is related to oxygen vacancies, the PL band of 2.50 eV is connected with oxygen interstitials and the PL band of orange color is related to oxygen interstitials as well.
the radiative defects in ZnO NCs are varied at aging and these defects are connected with the oxygen interstitials.

aging is connected with the formation of AgZn defects in ZnO NCs, which are responsible for the orange PL band, and the variation of AgZn and Ag-O defects at aging is the reason of the variation of the PL intensity in the UV-blue spectral range.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiative defects in ZnO NCs are not stable and change under the influence of thermal annealing.
the PL intensity of 3.18 and 2.70 bands decreases at aging and the intensity of 2.85 and 2.50 PL bands increases.
aging of ZnO NCs is accompanied by the formation of oxygen vacancies and oxygen interstitials.
